toc.title: Screening many routines for the slowest (gh-ocannl-1763, gh-ocannl-1818)

preamble:
Re-timing a shipped routine with a stated, measured spread (gh-ocannl-1524).

A runner that compiles a routine (a tuned winner, a model pick, an untuned default) and then reports how fast it runs used to time it min-of-N synchronized runs, once. On a kernel under ~50 us that single minimum is noise-dominated: on cc, gh-ocannl-1397's unchanged control site read 0.69x between two builds and a changed site 1.44x the wrong way, while the search's own best_ms (the tuner's queued protocol) agreed with itself to a few percent. Two things were missing, and this module supplies both:

  • The tuner's protocol. Each reading is one Autotune.time_routine call under the configured autotune_timing and autotune_repeats -- warmup, calibration to a ~10 ms batch (on cc and Metal up to 200 launches per synchronization), and a minimum over a top-up window -- so a re-timing measures the quantity a search ranked its candidates by, with the submit/sync round trip amortized rather than paid per reading.
  • A spread. A routine is read calls times, each call independent (its own warmup, calibration and window), and the report is the median of those readings with their range. Several routines are read in one session, interleaved in Bench_design's spread mirrored rotation, so a drift over the session lands on every routine alike; their ratio is PAIRED, call by call, and reported as the median paired ratio with its range. A ratio is resolved only when every pair agrees on its side of 1 -- with the default six calls, the exact two-sided sign-test p of that outcome is 2/64 = 0.031.

Below min_readings admitted readings a spread is not stated: its bounds are NaN and a ratio over it is never resolved. A reading the tuner's admission gate refuses (Autotune.admitted_timing_ms: host contention, an unbatched calibration, a clock that resolved nothing) is counted as refused and left out, never ranked.

Boundary: the spread is the session's -- what this process measured about routines it compiled. Two builds compared across processes (a base and a head) carry, on top, whatever differs between the processes (code placement, the tuned arm's crown); pair them through benchmarks/ab.py or benchmarks/bin_cells.py, round by round, and read each process's own spread beside the paired ratio.
content:
val min_readings : int
val calls_of_env : unit -> Base.Int.t

calls_of_env (): BENCH_RETIME_CALLS (default 6), the timing calls per routine. Even, because Bench_design mirrors every batch, and at least min_readings.

type spread = {
  1. ms : Base.float;
    (*

    The median admitted reading; NaN with none.

    *)
  2. lo_ms : Base.float;
    (*

    The least admitted reading; NaN below min_readings.

    *)
  3. hi_ms : Base.float;
    (*

    The greatest admitted reading; NaN below min_readings.

    *)
  4. admitted : Base.int;
  5. refused : Base.int;
}

One routine's re-timing: per-launch milliseconds, each reading one Autotune.time_routine call.

val median : Base.Float.t Base.Array.t -> Base.Float.t
val sorted_admitted : Base.Float.t option Base.Array.t -> Base.Float.t Base.Array.t
val spread_of : Base.float Base.option Base.array -> spread

spread_of readings: the summary of one routine's readings, None for a refused call.

val rel_spread : spread -> Base__Float.t

rel_spread s: (hi - lo) / median, the spread as a fraction of the reading; NaN unstated.

type ratio = {
  1. ratio : Base.float;
    (*

    The median of the paired ratios; NaN with no pair.

    *)
  2. ratio_lo : Base.float;
    (*

    The least paired ratio; NaN below min_readings pairs.

    *)
  3. ratio_hi : Base.float;
    (*

    The greatest paired ratio; NaN below min_readings pairs.

    *)
  4. pairs : Base.int;
    (*

    The calls at which both routines' readings were admitted.

    *)
  5. resolved : Base.bool;
    (*

    At least min_readings pairs and every paired ratio on one side of 1: the two routines differ by more than the session's noise. Unresolved is "within the spread", not "equal".

    *)
}
val paired_ratio : num:Base.float Base.option Base.array -> den:Base.float Base.option Base.array -> ratio

paired_ratio ~num ~den: num's readings over den's, call by call. The two arrays are two routines' readings from one retime session, index i of each taken in the same mirrored batch, so a drift common to the batch divides out.

val bounds_fields : name:string -> spread -> string

bounds_fields ~name s: name_lo=<ms> name_hi=<ms> name_retimed=<admitted>/<calls>, for a line that prints the median name=<ms> elsewhere.

val spread_fields : name:string -> spread -> string

spread_fields ~name s: name=<ms> then bounds_fields, the one spelling every runner's line uses.

val ratio_fields : name:string -> ratio -> string

ratio_fields ~name r: name=<r> name_lo=<r> name_hi=<r> name_resolved=<bool>.

val configured_timing : unit -> Autotune.timing_mode

The configured objective, read as Autotune.tune reads it.

val configured_repeats : unit -> Base.Int.t

retime ?calls routines: every routine's readings, calls (default calls_of_env) per routine, in Bench_design.orders' visiting order, each reading an independent Autotune.time_routine call under configured_timing and the configured autotune_repeats, admitted through Autotune.admitted_timing_ms. The result is in the input's order, one array of calls readings per routine, index i taken in batch i.

Timing dispatches each routine many times against its live buffers (Autotune.time_routine restores nothing), so a caller checking a routine's output runs it once more afterwards from inputs that are not its own outputs, as an exactness oracle must anyway.

val screen_reading : Base.Float.t -> Base.Float.t option

screen_reading ms: what a screen ranks one timing call by, given the call's minimum: the minimum whenever the clock resolved one, and None for a non-positive or non-finite one. It reads no admission verdict: a screen ranks a refused window by its minimum too -- see the screen's section below.

val read_screen : timing:Autotune.timing_mode -> (Context.t * Context.routine) -> Base.Float.t option * bool

read_screen ~timing (ctx, routine): one screen reading under timing and the configured autotune_repeats: (screen_reading ms, refused), refused when Autotune.admitted_timing_ms refused the window -- which rescreen's cut and the instrument's count read, and the reading does not.

val read_once : ?timing:??? -> (Context.t * Context.routine) -> Base.float Base.option

read_once (ctx, routine): one reading -- one Autotune.time_routine call under configured_timing and the configured autotune_repeats, admitted through Autotune.admitted_timing_ms (None when refused). retime is made of these.

val retime : ?calls:??? -> (Context.t * Context.routine) Base.list -> Autotune.timing_mode * Base.float option Base.Array.t list

Screening many routines for the slowest (gh-ocannl-1763, gh-ocannl-1818)

Re-timing every one of a step's kernels with a spread costs calls timing calls each, about half a second a call whatever the kernel's size: on a 178-kernel gpt2_mini_train step on Metal, about 2.1 s a kernel and 371-381 s of a 377-386 s cell. Only the slowest kernel's time is reported, so the many kernels that are nowhere near it need no spread: each is SCREENED with one reading (read_once), and only the kernels whose screen reading comes within screen_ratio of the slowest one -- at most screen_at_most of them -- are re-timed, together, in one retime session, where the slowest is decided by median with its range as before.

The screen runs in two stages (gh-ocannl-1818). One reading under the configured objective -- queued by default -- still cost 1.1-1.5 s on CUDA/HIP, where it calibrates a batch depth of up to 2048 launches with probes and confirmations, so a 270-kernel HIP step spent ~410 s of its 600 s budget on the screen alone. The first stage reads every kernel once under screen_timing, isolated -- one launch and one host synchronization a sample, no calibration -- and keeps the screen_wide_at_most slowest isolated readings, plus any kernel with no reading (screen_keep_wide); it applies no ratio, since a ratio between two isolated readings says nothing reliable about the configured objective's (two kernels of 8 and 7 us under queued timing can read 48 and 97 us isolated, their round trips differing). The second reads only those, once each, under the configured objective, and keeps the re-timing's candidates from THOSE readings (rescreen). An isolated reading carries a launch-and-sync round trip the queued objective amortizes (~40-90 us on gfx1151, varying by kernel), so it does not order kernels whose times are within that round trip of one another, and on a step whose dominant kernel is a few times the round trip the floor-bound kernels crowd the slowest isolated readings. The wide cap is what absorbs that: a kernel outranks the queued-slowest one in the first stage only by an isolated reading above it, and the final cap of screen_at_most is ranked by queued readings, which the round trip does not inflate.

A reading is a minimum over a window, so noise only raises it above the kernel's floor. The truly slowest kernel is therefore left out only when, in the first stage, screen_wide_at_most other kernels' isolated readings came out above its own, or, in the second, some other kernel's admitted reading came out more than twice its own -- an inflated window -- or screen_at_most others above it; and then a wrong one can be named.

A screen reading is ranked by its minimum even when Autotune.admitted_timing_ms refuses the window (screen_reading): the screen only decides what is re-measured, and a refused window's minimum can only over-state the kernel -- it is not dropped on a reading noise lowered, it may only crowd the cap as any inflated window does. It does not set the second stage's cut, though, while any reading there was admitted (rescreen): on CUDA/HIP a queued reading refused as unbatched is a depth-1, round-trip-inclusive time, and as the slowest it would cut a kernel whose admitted queued reading is the larger true time. Before gh-ocannl-1818 a refused reading was kept unconditionally, outside the cap, and on a shared box that made the screen's cost unbounded: a Metal gpt2_mini_train step under co-tenant load had 38 of 195 queued screen readings refused, and re-timed all 46 candidates at four calls each, 136 s; isolated, 105 of 195 were refused. Only a kernel with no reading at all -- a clock that resolved nothing -- is still kept outside the cap, since nothing is known of it. The re-timing's readings, which decide the dominant kernel and state its range, go through the admission gate as before.

val screen_timing : Autotune.timing_mode

The first stage's objective: isolated, whatever autotune_timing says, because it needs no calibration.

val screen_ratio : float

A kernel is a candidate when its screen reading is at least the slowest one over this.

val screen_at_most : int

The most screened kernels re-timed, the slowest readings first: on a step whose many kernels all read within screen_ratio of one another (identical layers), the cap keeps the re-timing bounded. Those left out read below every candidate, so the cap can mis-name the slowest only among kernels a single reading did not order -- ones whose re-timed ranges would most likely overlap anyway.

val screen_keep : ?ratio:??? -> ?at_most:??? -> ?refused:??? -> ('a * Base.Float.t Base.Option.t) Base.List.t -> 'a Base.List.t * 'a Base.List.t

screen_keep ?ratio ?at_most ?refused entries: (kept, dropped), each in entries' order, of entries paired with their screen reading (None: no reading). Kept: every entry with none, and of the others those reading at least slowest /. ratio (ratio default screen_ratio), at most at_most (default screen_at_most) of them, the slowest first, ties to the earlier entry. slowest is the slowest reading of an entry refused (default: none) does not hold, or, when it holds of every entry with a reading, the slowest of those.

Without refused, applied after each new reading to the entries kept so far, it keeps exactly what it keeps applied once to all of them: the slowest reading only grows, so an entry it drops stays below the final cut, and one dropped by the cap has at_most entries above it that are dropped, if ever, only for something that drops it too. So a caller may release what it drops as it goes. With refused the slowest can fall (an admitted reading arriving after refused ones only), so apply it once.

val screen_wide_at_most : Base__Int.t

The most kernels the first stage keeps (not counting those with no reading), the slowest isolated readings first: three times screen_at_most, so that the queued-slowest kernel stays in while fewer than that many others read above it isolated -- sixteen more than the final cap allows. Each costs one reading under the configured objective in the second stage: on minix (HIP, unified memory, gpt2_mini_train) the 24 queued calls took 25.8-25.9 s, about 1.1 s a call.

val rank_among : Base.Float.t -> Base.Float.t Base.List.t -> Base__Int.t

rank_among r readings: r's rank among readings, 1 for the slowest, ties sharing the better rank -- 1 + the readings above it. The instrument's closing line states the dominant kernel's rank among the re-screened kernels' isolated readings by it: how close the first stage came to leaving it out.

val screen_keep_wide : ('a * Base.Float.t Base.Option.t) Base.List.t -> 'a Base.List.t * 'a Base.List.t

screen_keep_wide entries: the first stage's cut, screen_keep at screen_wide_at_most and no ratio, over entries paired with their screen_timing reading. Like screen_keep without refused, it may be applied after each reading.

val rescreen : read:('a -> Base.Float.t Base.Option.t * Base.bool) -> 'a Base.List.t -> ('a * Base.Float.t Base.Option.t) Base.List.t * ('a * Base.Float.t Base.Option.t) Base.List.t

rescreen ~read entries: the second stage. Reads each of entries -- the first stage's kept set -- once with read (the configured objective's read_screen: the reading and whether the admission gate refused it), in entries' order, and returns (kept, dropped) of (entry, reading) by screen_keep at its defaults over those readings, the cut set by the admitted ones while there are any: what the re-timing gets, and what keeps its second-stage reading.
